nodes.summary: Two impartial games $G$ and $H$ are equivalent when no third game tells them apart as summands: for every impartial game $K$, the starting position of the sum $G + K$ is a P-position if and only if the starting position of the sum $H + K$ is a P-position. The starting position of a sum is the pair of the starting positions of its summands.
nodes.title: Equivalence of impartial games

nodes.summary: The sum $G + H$ of two impartial games $G$ and $H$ is the impartial game whose positions are the pairs $(a, b)$ of a position $a$ of $G$ and a position $b$ of $H$, and in which a move changes exactly one component: from $(a, b)$ one may move to $(a', b)$ for any move from $a$ to $a'$ in $G$, or to $(a, b')$ for any move from $b$ to $b'$ in $H$. Its starting position is the pair of the starting positions of $G$ and…
nodes.title: Sum of impartial games

nodes.summary: An impartial game consists of a type of positions, a starting position, for each position $p$ a finite set of positions reachable from $p$ in one move, and a rank function assigning a natural number to each position such that every move strictly decreases the rank: if $q$ is reachable from $p$ in one move, then $\mathrm{rank}(q) < \mathrm{rank}(p)$.
nodes.title: Impartial game

nodes.summary: In an impartial game $G$, a position $p$ is a P-position if and only if every position reachable from $p$ in one move is not a P-position.
nodes.title: Recursive characterization of P-positions

nodes.summary: In an impartial game $G$, the P-positions are defined by well-founded recursion along moves: a position $p$ is a P-position if and only if no position reachable from $p$ in one move is a P-position. Positions that are not P-positions are called N-positions.
nodes.title: P-positions

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Nim heap of size $n$ is the impartial game whose positions are $0, 1, \dots, n$, whose starting position is $n$, and in which a move from $k$ goes to any $j < k$; the rank of a position is its value.
nodes.title: Nim heap

nodes.summary: Write $x \to y$ when there is a move from position $x$ to position $y$, and assume there is no infinite sequence of moves $x_0 \to x_1 \to x_2 \to \cdots$. Call a set $P$ of positions stable if no move leads from a position in $P$ to a position in $P$, and absorbing if from every position outside $P$ some move leads to a position in $P$. Then any two stable and absorbing sets of positions are equal.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the P-positions of a terminating impartial game

nodes.summary: Every impartial game $G$ is equivalent to a Nim heap: there is a natural number $n$ such that $G$ is equivalent to the Nim heap of size $n$.
nodes.title: Sprague–Grundy theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
